found: 7 of the 10 covers were AI images, and no cover showed a person or a real piece.
Headlines read like riddles, with what Trove is in a small second line.
Every cover carried three blocks of text: headline, explainer and proposition.
The offer (free to join, we photograph it, we collect it) was hidden inside the carousels.
All ten covers shared one layout, so the grid would read as one ad repeated.
The shop page mock-up was full of dashed boxes.
"Made here. Made home." was a third tagline beside "Curated for Living" and the proposition.
changed: A new order: what Trove is (posts 1 to 3), then makers and providers get their own posts. Pin posts 1 to 3.
One headline of seven words or fewer and one short line on every cover, with the offer along the bottom.

No AI image on any cover except the Collection tease, which the brief allows. Covers that need real hands are labelled photo slots until the shoot; the rest are type cards or the real site on a phone.
Covers now alternate: real photo, type card, phone screen, Reel cover.

New: "We'd rather know who made it." (24 Oct) and "Makers. Providers. Buyers." (27 Oct). Dropped: "Someone in your building", "Who do you call?" and "Who's the one everyone asks?". Nominations are now a closing line: "Know a maker? Tag them."
A filled-in example shop page, labelled as an example, replaces the dashed mock-up. No invented maker.
"Made here. Made home." is only a small sign-off on end cards now.
Covers name three services (workshops, styling, photography), as the Sell page does. The full range stays inside the posts.
A renderer bug marked every list slide "Needs input". Fixed, so the ready count is now right.
declined: Dream Avenue headlines: Cormorant stays. You chose it on 27 July because Dream Avenue was never bought. The wordmark still swaps in when the file arrives.
Cutting services to workshops, styling and photography: lettering, repairs, gift wrapping and the rest are real categories on the site. Covers lead with three; the inside keeps the range.
"Free to join. Keep 60%." as a headline: your 19 Oct rule keeps money out of headlines. Post 9 keeps "What Trove costs, and what you keep." and the 60% stays inside.
"In a world of fast, throwaway things": the brief never knocks mass-made goods. The line is now "Pieces made with care, by people you can name."
"Handmade homeware" in the one-liner: Trove also takes jewellery, stationery, children's and pet pieces, so it says "handmade pieces".
Kiln & Clay: it was a test shop, removed from the live site on 15 Oct, and it isn't in any post.

campaign.manifesto:
Some of us were born here. Some of us came from far away.
Either way, home is something we make.
A cushion cover stitched in the evenings.
A chair brought back to life at the weekend.
The lettering on every wedding card in the family.
Here, home is made by hand: by neighbours, by friends, by people you can name.
Trove is a new online marketplace for handmade pieces and creative services in Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
We take the photographs. A courier comes to your door. You keep making.
Made here. Made home.

posts.title: Handmade in Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
posts.cover: Higgsfield image: hands finishing an embroidered linen cushion, close up (real shot 1 replaces it)
posts.drives: Understanding what Trove is, then applications
posts.caption: Trove is a new online marketplace for handmade pieces and creative services in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Makers sell what they make by hand: ceramics, candles, textiles, prints, jewellery and more. Providers take bookings for workshops, home styling and photography. Makers join free, and providers list free during launch. We photograph your pieces, or you use your own, and a courier collects each sale from your door. Make something, or offer a service? Apply in about ten minutes at troveathome.com/apply. Looking to buy? Follow along: the Marketplace opens to buyers soon.

posts.title: Make things by hand? You're a maker.

posts.for: People who make things by hand, including those who have never sold
posts.caption: If you make things by hand, you're a maker, whether you've sold a hundred pieces or none. On Trove you get your own shop page with your name and story. It's free to join, and there's nothing to pay if nothing sells. Our photographer can shoot your pieces, and a courier collects each sale from your door in Dubai or Abu Dhabi. Four lovely pieces is a shop. Apply in about ten minutes at troveathome.com/apply. Know a maker? Tag them.

posts.drives: Understanding exactly how Trove works, then applications
posts.caption: Here's exactly what Trove does. You make at your own pace and set your price. We photograph your pieces, or you use your own photos, and they go on your own shop page on troveathome.com. When something sells, Trove books a courier to collect it from your door in Dubai or Abu Dhabi, packed in your own packaging. Your Instagram and markets stay yours. Have ready photos of your work, a WhatsApp number and rough prices, then apply at troveathome.com/apply. Know a maker? Tag them.

posts.title: What Trove costs, and what you keep.
posts.cover: Higgsfield image: a maker's hands tying a blank price tag to a vase

posts.caption: Money and paperwork, plainly. Pieces: nothing to join, nothing to pay if nothing sells, you set the price and keep 60%, paid every other Tuesday after the 15-day return window. Services: free to list during launch, then AED 30 a month with 30 days' notice; you keep 100% when paid directly, or 90% by card through Trove. Anything we missed? shoot.intro: Book it this week: five covers wait on it (posts 1, 2, 4, 7 and 8), and post 10 needs a real founding maker. One afternoon, 14:00 to dusk, in two homes (an apartment and a villa, or a home and its building corridor). Three or four consenting friends, family or team members who genuinely make or mend things, using their real craft. They are never presented as Trove makers; the only credit is "Filmed with friends of Trove at home in [area]". Offer hands-only to everyone up front.

shoot.rules: No house numbers, street signs or car plates. No children's faces. No flag or emblem. Ask before filming in a majlis or any private room.
release: Who is filming (Trove, a brand of Serein Consultancy LLC), the date and place.
What is recorded, with ticks for face, hands only, voice, first name shown and neighbourhood shown. Never the address.
Where it is used: Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, the website, paid ads (if so) and printed postcards.
For how long, and that they can withdraw: future use stops and Trove removes its own posts within [7] days.
They are never described as a Trove maker unless they apply and are approved, and they see the final edit first.
Their work stays theirs. No payment, and no obligation to apply.
The person responsible for the home agrees to the interiors being filmed. No under-18s.
Have a UAE lawyer check the form, in English and Arabic.

siteFixes: The Apply form won't submit without an Instagram or a website link.

Every post sends people to Apply, and this campaign speaks to hobbyists who often have neither. The review agrees this is the most important fix. Options: let them tick "I don't have either yet" and send photos by WhatsApp, or keep the rule and soften the posts. Your call; Claude can build the first option.
The homepage says "independent makers across the UAE".
Trove is Dubai and Abu Dhabi only. It is also in the Site content defaults. Suggested: "independent makers in Dubai and Abu Dhabi".
The Collection band on the homepage says the Marketplace "is full of handmade pieces".
It has no pieces yet. Suggested: "Until the first pieces land, the Trove Marketplace is opening to makers in Dubai and Abu Dhabi."
series: A 30-second collab Reel following a real person here from "it's just a hobby" to their own shop page on Trove. Post 10 is the first.
One handmade thing in a real home in Dubai or Abu Dhabi, and the person who made it. Followers join in with an Add Yours sticker, so every tag is a nomination.
A provider at work in someone's home: a table set, a bowl mended, a workshop. Host and provider both repost.
nomination: Ways in: the closing line on maker and provider posts ("Know a maker? Tag them."), a tag in the comments, the Add Yours sticker or #WhoMadeThatTrove, a "Who should we meet?" question sticker, or a DM with a name.
Log every name in one shared sheet: handle, who nominated them, craft or service, area, date and status.
Check they are in Dubai or Abu Dhabi and that their work is something Trove accepts. If not, reply warmly to the nominator only.
Thank the nominator: "Thank you, we'll say hello."
A person writes to the nominee within two working days, after looking at their work. Name the nominator only if they tagged in public; otherwise ask the nominator first.
Follow up once after seven days, then stop.
If the nominee applies and agrees, tell the nominator. A founding maker's spotlight can thank their nominator by name, with both people's consent. No paid rewards.
